payload.title: partialPolicy declared at coordination session open causes the FIRST completed required pass to…
payload.description: partialPolicy declared at coordination session open causes the FIRST completed required pass to auto-close the session to a terminal status, permanently blocking any later fix-round authorization on that session. Kernel bug in session-engine.mjs's auto-close-after-every-call path and schema.mjs's validatePartialPolicy. HIGH risk: hit independently twice in the architecture-advisory-panel track (P00.1, P01.1) and affects any declared-protocol session using partialPolicy for a legitimate partial-completion escape hatch while also needing a fix round -- shared by fgos-code-panel and fgos-group-thinking's own protocol pack members, not unique to one track. Fix must refuse to auto-close to a terminal status while a fix round is still authorizable under the protocol's own graph, while still permitting the escape hatch partialPolicy exists for when no fix round is coming. Found and documented in docs/architect/agent-coordination/verification/architecture-advisory-panel/P02.1.md Table 4 BL1.

payload.title: dispatch.mjs decide/execute treats 3 track-proven-safe, allowlisted executor labels (claude-bwrap,…
payload.description: dispatch.mjs decide/execute treats 3 track-proven-safe, allowlisted executor labels (claude-bwrap, agy-bwrap, codex-readonly) as unregistered, forcing every advisory dispatch of them to bypass the dispatch door's own safety/audit trail entirely. Not a legality failure by itself (the manual bwrap/codex invocation this track uses is independently proven safe in P00.1), but it means the door's audit trail is silently skipped for exactly the executors this track trusts most. Fix location: .fgos/config.json executor registry (config, not code), or src/runner/dispatch/resolve.mjs's fallback logic if more than config is needed. Registering the 3 pairs must not silently widen what ANY other caller of dispatch.mjs decide can reach -- must be additive registration of already-proven-safe pairs, not a policy relaxation. Found and documented in docs/architect/agent-coordination/verification/architecture-advisory-panel/P02.1.md Table 4 BL2.

payload.title: src/verbs/coordination/schema.mjs's assertSafeRefOrId refuses ANY…
payload.description: src/verbs/coordination/schema.mjs's assertSafeRefOrId refuses ANY contribution:/human-turn:-prefixed disposition ref at the charset check, for every declared protocol -- so a disposition can never legally cite a real human turn or a deliberation contribution through fgos coordination run (the request-file door), even though the store-layer door (recordDriverDisposition, assertDispositionRefOwnedBySession) fully supports both ref namespaces. Fix: assertSafeRefOrId (or wherever the charset check lives) needs to allow the already-safe contribution: and human-turn: prefixes through to the ref-ownership check, matching what the store layer already accepts. Documented in docs/architect/agent-coordination/verification/architecture-advisory-panel/proofs/P03.2/doer-report.md.

payload.title: No specialist-authorize request-step type exists for fgos coordination run (the…
payload.description: No specialist-authorize request-step type exists for fgos coordination run (the request-file/pack-gate door) -- same class of gap as the pre-existing contribution/human-turn request-step limitation. payload.title: In the coordination engine, a declared-protocol session's actors[] roster (per-actor…
payload.description: In the coordination engine, a declared-protocol session's actors[] roster (per-actor executor/tier/persona overrides) is read fresh from each fgos coordination run request only -- run.mjs's findActor(request.actors, ...) never persists it to the session manifest and never reads it back on a later resumed call. Verified live: opening a session with actors[] binding a role to a confined executor (e.g. claude-bwrap), then a second, separate CLI invocation resuming the SAME coordinationId but omitting actors[] entirely, silently dispatches that role through the global default executor instead -- with no warning, no refusal. In this repo that default currently resolves to an unconfined, git-write-capable claude invocation (--permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools Bash(git add:*),Bash(git commit:*)). This is the same class of risk as tsk-1o4 (silent fallback to an unconfined executor) but for a different mechanism: tsk-1o4 is about unregistered executor names falling back; this is about a CORRECTLY-registered, CORRECTLY-confined roster silently losing its own confinement on any later call that forgets to repeat actors[] verbatim. Found and confirmed independently by both the Doer and Red-Team while building/attacking the architecture-advisory-panel-v1 skill's P04.2 examples (see docs/architect/agent-coordination/verification/architecture-advisory-panel/proofs/P04.2/ for both independent confirmations, including exact run.mjs line numbers). Currently worked around by prose discipline only (the how-to guide now tells callers to repeat actors[] on every call) -- Red-Team's own assessment: 'repeat it every call or lose confinement is a sharp edge prose won't hold across many sessions.' Real fix options: persist the opening roster onto the session manifest and use it as the default for later calls unless explicitly overridden, or refuse (rather than silently downgrade) a resumed dispatch for an actor that was previously confined and is now unbound.
payload.verify: chưa xác định — P15 bổ sung

payload.title: Crash-killed coordination dispatch leaves a stale dispatch.claim lock blocking CLI-only resume
payload.verify: Repro: kill -9 a real 'fgos coordination run' process mid-dispatch (after createSessionAssignment, during executeAssignment), confirm process dead, then re-run the identical operation step through the CLI -- observe 'a dispatch is already in progress' refusal citing the stale dispatch.claim file; fix should let 'fgos coordination show'/'run' detect and safely reconcile a claim whose owning process is verifiably dead, without requiring direct filesystem access to the .fgos/assignments/<id>/dispatch.claim file.
payload.description: Found live during P05.1's real crash/fresh-process-resume proof (architecture-advisory-panel track, group-thinking-plan-loop branch): session-engine.mjs's createAndExecuteSessionTask deliberately fails closed on a SIGKILL'd in-flight dispatch (see its own doc comment: 'a crashed in-flight dispatch still needs manual reconciliation, not silent auto-retry'), by design, not a defect in that function. But the ONLY reconciliation path today is direct filesystem access (rm the dispatch.claim file after confirming the OS-level PID is dead) -- there is no fgos coordination CLI door (run/show/chain) that detects a claim's owning process is dead and clears it. This means the SKILL.md/coordinator-facing promise that a fresh agent can resume a crashed session 'using only fgos coordination show/chain plus the session id' is incomplete for this one failure mode: a genuine process crash mid-dispatch requires an operator with filesystem access, not just the documented CLI doors. Full repro, exact commands/output, and the manual-reconciliation workaround that DOES work are in docs/architect/agent-coordination/verification/architecture-advisory-panel/proofs/P05.1/crash-state-snapshot.md and doer-report.md (Area 6).

payload.title: findLatestRunResult (src/runner/coordination/session-engine.mjs:262) reads runs/<n>/result.json…
payload.description: findLatestRunResult (src/runner/coordination/session-engine.mjs:262) reads runs/<n>/result.json off disk and trusts it as the genuine RunResult with NO shape validation and NO authenticity/cross-check against what the engine itself actually dispatched (which executor/provider/model/tier was requested, or whether an executor subprocess even ran). Verified live during P05.1's red-team round: hand-writing a result.json claiming a different executor/provider/tier than the one actually requested was accepted and linked as genuine provenance, exit 0, zero executors spawned. This is a real cross-trust-boundary vulnerability, not a same-privilege-as-coordinator issue: executor subprocesses run with cwd=workspace and can read/write ANY assignment directory including ones that are not their own (a separate but related finding -- assignment directories are not filesystem-isolated from each other or from the executors dispatched into them), so the LEAST trusted actor in the system (a dispatched executor, effectively running arbitrary LLM-driven tool calls) can fabricate or overwrite another assignment's result.json and have the engine report it as real dispatch provenance. This undermines the routing/provenance guarantee this whole coordination engine's heterogeneous-dispatch and distinct-model-per-tier claims depend on (used throughout the architecture-advisory-panel track: P00.1's admitted allowlist, P03.2's real distinct-model conformance assertion, P04.1/P04.2's heterogeneous-roster claims) -- those claims were made in good faith without an active adversary and are not false, but they were never adversarially hardened against this. Fix: validate result.json's shape and cross-check its claimed executor/provider/tier against the engine's own dispatch-plan/run.json record (what was ACTUALLY requested/spawned for that specific run attempt) before linking it as genuine; also close the underlying filesystem-isolation gap (an executor subprocess should not be able to read/write assignment directories other than its own). Found and reproduced live by Red-Team during docs/architect/agent-coordination/verification/architecture-advisory-panel/proofs/P05.1/ (F1 and F8 in redteam-findings.json).
payload.verify: chưa xác định — P15 bổ sung

payload.title: revise-synthesis (and by the same mechanism, revise-explanation) in the coordination engine's…
payload.description: revise-synthesis (and by the same mechanism, revise-explanation) in the coordination engine's declared-protocol graph is documented/intended as spendable only once a real human turn has been recorded and a real synthesis exists to revise -- but this precondition is prose-only, not kernel-enforced. Verified live by Red-Team (docs/architect/agent-coordination/verification/architecture-advisory-panel/proofs/P05.1/, finding F5): the operation was successfully authorized AND dispatched with ZERO human turns recorded and ZERO prior synthesis in the session, skipping the entire intended graph sequencing. Only the activation.maxInvocations CAP is kernel-enforced (confirmed real and working in the same round); the PRECONDITION that gates when the cap-limited operation may be invoked at all is not. Fix: the driver-authorization door for a bounded-reopen-class operation (revise-synthesis, revise-explanation, and any future operation of the same shape) should refuse authorization when its own documented precondition (e.g. 'requires at least one recorded human-turn ref' or 'requires a prior instance of the operation it revises') is not met, rather than relying on the authorizing driver to know and respect that rule.
payload.verify: chưa xác định — P15 bổ sung

payload.title: aggregateBounds declared on a resumed fgos coordination run request is silently discarded in both…
payload.description: aggregateBounds declared on a resumed fgos coordination run request is silently discarded in both directions -- neither tightening nor loosening the session's originally-declared bounds has any effect, exit 0, no warning, no error. Verified live by Red-Team (docs/architect/agent-coordination/verification/architecture-advisory-panel/proofs/P05.1/, finding F6). Consequence: a session opened with an under-budgeted aggregateBounds.maxRounds (or any other bound) that turns out to need more rounds -- e.g. the exact class of bug this same track's P04.2 cell found and fixed in its own documentation, and P05.1's own live proof needed maxRounds:12 minimum for one reopen -- becomes PERMANENTLY WEDGED once opened: there is no CLI door to raise the bound after the fact, and a resumed request that tries to is silently ignored rather than refused or honored. Fix: either allow a resumed request to legitimately raise (never lower, to avoid retroactively shrinking an already-in-progress session's headroom) aggregateBounds via an explicit, audited mechanism, or at minimum REFUSE (rather than silently ignore) a resumed request that attempts to change aggregateBounds from its original declared value, so the caller knows the change had no effect instead of believing it worked.

patch.description:
Found live during P05.1's real crash/fresh-process-resume proof (architecture-advisory-panel track, group-thinking-plan-loop branch): session-engine.mjs's createAndExecuteSessionTask deliberately fails closed on a SIGKILL'd in-flight dispatch (see its own doc comment: 'a crashed in-flight dispatch still needs manual reconciliation, not silent auto-retry'), by design, not a defect in that function. But the ONLY reconciliation path today is direct filesystem access (rm the dispatch.claim file after confirming the OS-level PID is dead) -- there is no fgos coordination CLI door (run/show/chain) that detects a claim's owning process is dead and clears it. This means the SKILL.md/coordinator-facing promise that a fresh agent can resume a crashed session 'using only fgos coordination show/chain plus the session id' is incomplete for this one failure mode: a genuine process crash mid-dispatch requires an operator with filesystem access, not just the documented CLI doors.

CORRECTION, added after independent Red-Team re-attack (same proof round, findings F2/F3 in docs/architect/agent-coordination/verification/architecture-advisory-panel/proofs/P05.1/redteam-findings.json): the fix premise above ("a claim whose owning process is verifiably dead") is NOT implementable as stated. `dispatch.claim` is a zero-byte file -- it records no PID, host, or owner identity anywhere, and no file under the assignment records one either. The Doer's own manual-reconciliation demo only worked because they had insider knowledge from their own test harness's marker file, not from anything a real incident responder could read. Any real fix must FIRST add owner identity (PID, host, start-time) to the claim record before "verify it's dead" can mean anything.

Two related, WORSE failure modes found in the same round, not covered by the above and worth fixing together since they touch the same lock/reconciliation surface:
- F2: if a stale dispatch.claim is removed while the underlying per-cwd dispatch lock (src/runner/dispatch/cli.mjs:467-474, `releaseOnExit: true`, real repo config `timeoutMs: 2100000` = 35 minutes) is STILL held (SIGKILL defeats `releaseOnExit` too), re-running does not fail cleanly -- the engine writes a `status: "failed"` RunResult and LINKS it. The actor flips `late` -> `failed` PERMANENTLY: every later run short-circuits at `priorLink` and returns that cached failure forever. `retrySessionTask` exists in the engine but no CLI door reaches it. The documented "recovery" workaround can therefore make things categorically worse if attempted inside the 35-minute lock-TTL window -- which is also exactly when an operator would naturally attempt it.
- F3: a SIGKILL during the event-log append itself (a narrower timing window than F2, but real) leaves the log in a shape where BOTH `fgos coordination show` and `fgos coordination run` exit 5 -- the session becomes undiagnosable, not merely unrecoverable. `events.mjs` already has a `repair()` function for exactly this shape, but no CLI door exposes it.

Real fix now needs, in order: (1) record real owner identity (PID/host/start-time) on dispatch.claim acquisition so "is the owner dead" becomes answerable; (2) a CLI door (`fgos coordination show`/`run`/a new subcommand) that detects a claim whose recorded owner is verifiably dead and safely reconciles it, without touching the per-cwd dispatch lock's own TTL semantics or requiring direct filesystem access; (3) expose `events.mjs`'s existing `repair()` through a CLI door for the F3 log-corruption case; (4) once (1)-(3) exist, either expose `retrySessionTask` through a CLI door or make reconciliation call it automatically so a `late`->`failed` mislink from a race during recovery can itself be corrected.

Full repro, exact commands/output, and evidence for all three failure modes are in docs/architect/agent-coordination/verification/architecture-advisory-panel/proofs/P05.1/crash-state-snapshot.md, doer-report.md (Area 6), and redteam-findings.json/redteam-report.md (F2, F3).

patch.description:
Found live during P05.1's real crash/fresh-process-resume proof (architecture-advisory-panel track, group-thinking-plan-loop branch): session-engine.mjs's createAndExecuteSessionTask deliberately fails closed on a SIGKILL'd in-flight dispatch (see its own doc comment: 'a crashed in-flight dispatch still needs manual reconciliation, not silent auto-retry'), by design, not a defect in that function. CORRECTION 1, added after independent Red-Team re-attack (same proof round, findings F2/F3 in docs/architect/agent-coordination/verification/architecture-advisory-panel/proofs/P05.1/redteam-findings.json): the fix premise above ("a claim whose owning process is verifiably dead") is NOT implementable as stated. `dispatch.claim` is a zero-byte file -- it records no PID, host, or owner identity anywhere, and no file under the assignment records one either. Any real fix must FIRST add owner identity (PID, host, start-time) to the claim record before "verify it's dead" can mean anything.

Two related, WORSE failure modes found in the same round, not covered by the above and worth fixing together since they touch the same lock/reconciliation surface:
- F2: if a stale dispatch.claim is removed while the underlying per-cwd dispatch lock (src/runner/dispatch/cli.mjs:480, `releaseOnExit: true`) is STILL held, re-running does not fail cleanly -- the engine writes a `status: "failed"` RunResult and LINKS it. The actor flips `late` -> `failed` PERMANENTLY: every later run short-circuits at `priorLink` and returns that cached failure forever. `retrySessionTask` exists in the engine but no CLI door reaches it.

CORRECTION 2 (Red-Team's own upward self-correction after re-verifying their report against this repo's real config, not their sandbox's): the F2 exposure window is NOT "only while the orphan executor happens to still be running" -- it is a DETERMINISTIC 35-minute window in this repo's real configuration, unconditionally. `main-checkout-lock.mjs`'s `tryAcquireOnce` judges lock validity by TTL freshness ALONE, with NO PID-liveness probe -- `cli.mjs` acquires the lock with `ttlMs: cfg.timeoutMs`, and this repo's real `.fgos/config.json` sets `runner.timeoutMs: 2100000` (= 2,100,000 ms = exactly 35 minutes). So after ANY SIGKILL of an in-flight dispatch, the second lock reads as validly held for the full 35 minutes regardless of whether the owning process is alive or dead -- and any resume attempted inside that window (which is exactly when an operator would naturally attempt one, right after confirming the process is dead) hits the permanent-poisoning failure mode described in F2 above. Real fix now needs, in order: (1) record real owner identity (PID/host/start-time) on dispatch.claim acquisition so "is the owner dead" becomes answerable; (2) add a PID-liveness probe to main-checkout-lock.mjs's own validity check (or an equivalent mechanism) so a SIGKILL'd owner's lock does not read as validly held for the full 35-minute TTL; (3) a CLI door (`fgos coordination show`/`run`/a new subcommand) that detects a claim whose recorded owner is verifiably dead and safely reconciles it, without requiring direct filesystem access; (4) expose `events.mjs`'s existing `repair()` through a CLI door for the F3 log-corruption case; (5) once (1)-(4) exist, either expose `retrySessionTask` through a CLI door or make reconciliation call it automatically so a `late`->`failed` mislink from a race during recovery can itself be corrected.

Full repro, exact commands/output, and evidence for all failure modes are in docs/architect/agent-coordination/verification/architecture-advisory-panel/proofs/P05.1/crash-state-snapshot.md, doer-report.md (Area 6, "Corrected conclusion" table), and redteam-findings.json/redteam-report.md (F2, F3, and F2's own appended correction).

payload.title: agy -p (headless/print mode) ignores the invoking OS process cwd entirely and defaults to a stale…
payload.description: agy -p (headless/print mode) ignores the invoking OS process cwd entirely and defaults to a stale internal scratch workspace (observed: ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/scratch, containing a leftover file from an unrelated prior probe) instead of the directory it was actually spawned in. Confirmed with BOTH an unconfined agy -p call and a bwrap --ro-bind / / confined call from the same real git repo directory -- identical wrong behavior in both, so this is not a sandboxing side effect, it is agy's own default workspace resolution. The fix is --add-dir <path>, which does correctly report the real cwd, list its real files, and read its real README.md content -- confirmed live. This directly affects the already-registered executors.agy-cli / executors.agy-herdr (.fgos/config.json), which declare --new-project but never --add-dir or any per-dispatch path: if their real dispatch relies on OS cwd alone (as .fgos/config.json's own agy-cli/agy-herdr templates do -- no --add-dir anywhere), any headless agy dispatch may silently operate on a stale unrelated scratch directory instead of the intended target repo, a correctness risk far more severe than a safety one (the agent isn't reading what the caller thinks it's reading). Found while registering a read-only-confined agy-bwrap executor for architecture-advisory-panel P05.2 dispatch (docs/architect/agent-coordination/verification/architecture-advisory-panel/proofs/P05.2/). Fix direction: transport.mjs's arg substitution only supports {prompt}/{model} (src/runner/dispatch/transport.mjs:160) -- extending it to also substitute a {cwd} token, then adding --add-dir {cwd} to agy-cli/agy-herdr/agy-bwrap's args, would let every agy dispatch declare its real target directory explicitly rather than relying on an assumption that has now been shown false. Not yet fixed -- P05.2 is proceeding with only 2 heterogeneous executor bindings (claude-bwrap, codex-readonly) rather than blocking on this.
payload.verify: chưa xác định — P15 bổ sung

payload.title: renderAssignmentPrompt (src/runner/dispatch/assignment.mjs:643) tells a dispatched worker WHERE to…
payload.description: renderAssignmentPrompt (src/runner/dispatch/assignment.mjs:643) tells a dispatched worker WHERE to write its result (absolute agent-result.json/agent-report.md paths, added per Step 04 5.1) but never explains WHAT SHAPE that JSON must take -- the allowed status enum (done|blocked|failed|no-evidence, assignment.mjs's ALLOWED_AGENT_CLAIM_STATUSES), the required summary field, or the conditional blocker/error fields. A real advisory-panel dispatch (architecture-advisory-panel-v1, P05.2) with no taskSpec set (a bare declared-protocol operation, objective text only) produced a substantive, correct, high-quality real answer but wrote status: "DONE_WITH_CONCERNS" -- a plausible status string from a DIFFERENT, unrelated convention (orchestration-protocol.md's own DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT) -- and failed schema validation outright (assignment-runner.mjs: "agent-result.json was present but failed schema validation", producing status:failed instead of accepting real, usable evidence). Any dispatch relying on renderAssignmentPrompt's own default template, without a taskSpec doc separately explaining the schema, is exposed to this: real analytical work done correctly, discarded on a naming mismatch the worker was never told about. Fix direction: renderAssignmentPrompt's 'Result artifact:' block (assignment.mjs:685-692) should also state the exact required shape (status enum, required summary, conditional blocker/error) inline, not rely on a taskSpec to carry it -- the coding domain's own task-specs already explain this per-domain, but any protocol/operation without one (e.g. a fresh declared-protocol coordination session) currently gets no schema guidance at all. Found live while dispatching P05.2 (architecture-advisory-panel P05.2, forgentX).
payload.verify: chưa xác định — P15 bổ sung

patch.description:
UPDATE (P05.2, still real, not closed): the underlying defect is confirmed unchanged -- agy -p genuinely ignores OS-level cwd for RELATIVE path resolution, defaulting to a stale internal scratch workspace regardless of confinement. But a live retest found a real, usable workaround: when given ABSOLUTE paths directly in the prompt (both for reading a file and for writing its own result file), agy correctly follows them -- read a real file's exact content via absolute path, wrote a probe file into a bwrap-writable exception via absolute path, and was correctly blocked (read-only filesystem, reported honestly) from mutating a repo via absolute path. So the defect is specifically agy's own RELATIVE "current directory" resolution, not its file I/O in general.

Practical consequence for any caller: any dispatch prompt built for agy (agy-cli/agy-herdr/agy-bwrap) must use absolute paths throughout -- objective text, context refs, everything -- never assume relative-to-cwd resolution will work, even though the OS-level cwd is set correctly (confirmed via run.json's own cwd field). A prompt written assuming ordinary relative-path CLI conventions (as every other registered executor here correctly supports) will silently operate on the wrong directory for agy specifically.

Original description retained below for the still-unfixed underlying defect (agy-cli/agy-herdr's own args templates still declare no absolute-path convention or --add-dir at all):

agy -p (headless/print mode) ignores the invoking OS process cwd entirely and defaults to a stale internal scratch workspace (observed: ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/scratch, containing a leftover file from an unrelated prior probe) instead of the directory it was actually spawned in. Confirmed with BOTH an unconfined agy -p call and a bwrap read-only-mounted confined call from the same real git repo directory -- identical wrong behavior in both, so this is not a sandboxing side effect, it is agy's own default workspace resolution. This directly affects the already-registered executors.agy-cli / executors.agy-herdr (.fgos/config.json), which rely on relative-path prompts working via OS cwd -- a real risk for any existing caller that has not already worked around it by using absolute paths.

payload.title: assignment-runner.mjs's mutation-detection (evidence.json's gitBefore/gitAfter +…
payload.description: assignment-runner.mjs's mutation-detection (evidence.json's gitBefore/gitAfter + dirtyBefore/dirtyAfter diff) is not causally isolated: it attributes ANY change to the cwd's git working tree between dispatch start/end to the dispatched executor, with no way to tell a real confinement breach apart from an unrelated concurrent editor touching the same repo during the same wall-clock window. Confirmed live during P05.2 (architecture-advisory-panel): a claude-bwrap dispatch (fully read-only OS mount, confirmed safe by repeated live attack-probe testing) against a real external project (herdr-gateway) produced a correct, schema-valid, on-topic agent-result.json (status: done) about block-classify.ts strategy, but the run's own evidence.json showed web/test/terminal.test.ts newly dirty after the run -- a real file mutation, unrelated in content to anything the dispatch's own prompt discussed (zero mentions of that file or its test names anywhere in the dispatch's own stdout/report/result). The machine had ~16 other long-running claude --dangerously-skip-permissions processes active at the time, and the target repo's OTHER file (web/src/views/terminal.ts) was already dirty BEFORE this dispatch even started -- strong evidence a different, unrelated, concurrent session was actively editing the same repo, and the framework's own before/after diff simply caught that unrelated edit and blamed it on this dispatch, overriding a correct agentClaim (status: done) into status: failed. Any advisory (or other) dispatch against a real project that has ANY other concurrent editor -- a live developer, another agent session, a CI job -- is exposed to this same false-failure class, and conversely a genuine confinement breach happening to land during a quiet window could be missed if evidence.json only checks git state, not what the confined process itself actually touched. Fix direction: evidence.json's mutation check needs some causal narrowing beyond a bare before/after git diff of the whole cwd -- e.g. correlating against the confined process's own file-access trace (strace/audit, or bwrap's own event log if bind-mounted with logging), or at minimum flagging in the result when other filesystem activity in cwd was independently detected during the dispatch window, so a false failed/failed is distinguishable from a real one instead of looking identical. Found and analyzed in docs/architect/agent-coordination/verification/architecture-advisory-panel/proofs/P05.2/.
payload.verify: chưa xác định — P15 bổ sung

payload.title: CoordinationSession's aggregateBounds carries a THIRD bound beyond the two already documented…
payload.description: CoordinationSession's aggregateBounds carries a THIRD bound beyond the two already documented (maxRounds, maxAssignments): wallTimeMs, defaulting to 3600000 (1 hour, DEFAULT_AGGREGATE_BOUNDS, src/runner/coordination/schema.mjs:76). Neither the fgos-architecture-panel how-to guide nor SKILL.md's own aggregateBounds guidance (which explicitly walks through raising maxRounds/maxAssignments for this exact protocol) ever mentions wallTimeMs -- a caller who only reads that guidance and declares {maxRounds, maxAssignments} still silently inherits the 1-hour wall-clock default. Confirmed live during P05.2: a real session with maxRounds/maxAssignments budget still unused hit 'wall-time budget (aggregateBounds.wallTimeMs: 3600000ms) has elapsed... refusing to materialize a new Assignment' (dispatchDeclaredOperation) purely because real-world delays (two OOM kills from unrelated system memory pressure, investigation time) pushed the session's wall-clock age past an hour -- unrelated to how much real dispatch work the session had actually done. Like maxRounds/maxAssignments, once elapsed this appears to have no CLI retry/extension door -- a new session is the only way forward, same class of gap as tsk-47l's crash-recovery finding and P05.1's own maxRounds discovery, but for a third, previously-undocumented bound. Fix direction: SKILL.md/the how-to guide's aggregateBounds section should name all three fields (maxRounds, maxAssignments, wallTimeMs) together, since a caller who reasons only from the documented two will be silently exposed to the third exactly when a session runs long for reasons unrelated to work volume (waiting on a person, resource contention, retries after a false-positive).
